narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>I think the line between the numbers was always there.
<bookmark mark='later'/>The line came much later, added by Al-Hassar, a mathematician from Morocco.
<bookmark mark='travel'/>The Indian way of writing travelled through the Arabs, and later reached Europe.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>The first Indian fractions had no line at all.

narration: <bookmark mark='name'/>Remember the old name bhinna, a broken whole made of equal parts.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>Brahmagupta also gave the rule we use to add fractions with the same unit.
<bookmark mark='turn'/>Your turn. How would an old Indian scholar write three fourths?
